findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher is broken: reversed logic and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The new `isAccessTokenId` matcher is supposed to verify that an access token id has the form `<sessionType 2><tokenType 2><grantType 2>:<uuid>` and that the grant shortcut equals `expectedGrantShortcut`. Instead, `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts index 3 (last char of token type) and index 4 (first char of grant type), so it never matches any real 2-char grant shortcut — for the existing grants it virtually never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, so the `if (...) return false;` early-out is never taken. And the logic is inverted: to require equality one must write `if (!substring.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, not `if (substring.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. The correct read should be `items[0].substring(4, 6)`. As a result every newly updated `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` event assertion silently degrades to a plain UUID check on the suffix, so the integration tests do not actually validate the grant type encoded into the access token id by the new SPI. A regression in the encoding (wrong prefix, wrong grant mapping) would slip through CI undetected.

findings.title: AccessTokenContext constructor never validates rawTokenId for null
findings.body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — a copy-paste of the previous line: it again checks `grantType` and uses a wrong error message. The intended `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` is missing. The promised non-null contract on `rawTokenId` is therefore not enforced. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` then happily appends `'null'` after the ':' producing malformed ids (e.g. `onrtac:null`), and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` on the receiver side gets back `null` for `rawTokenId`, breaking the round-trip and any later lookup logic that depends on the real jti.

findings.title: getShortcut() Javadoc says "3-letters" but codec uses a fixed 2-char position
findings.body: The new method's Javadoc reads "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` always splits the encoded id at fixed 2-char positions (`substring(4, 6)` for grant type) and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` enforces `encodedContext.length() != 6`. A shortcut of any length other than 2 will produce ids the default provider cannot decode (`IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6"`), and `encodeTokenId` will silently write the wrong number of characters. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` also does not enforce a 2-char length on `getShortcut()`, so an implementer that follows the documented 3-letter contract will only fail at runtime when an access token is issued or introspected. Either the Javadoc must be updated to "2-letter shortcut, unique across grants" or the codec must be generalised and the runtime length check removed.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds a new abstract method (breaking SPI change with no default)
findings.body: `String getShortcut();` was added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` as a fully abstract method with no default implementation. Every in-repo extension (AuthorizationCode, ClientCredentials, Refresh, ResourceOwnerPassword, TokenExchange, CIBA, Device, PreAuthorizedCode, Permission, plus any downstream implementations) is now required to implement it. Any third-party grant factory (token-exchange variants, custom grants, RAR-based extensions that Keycloak explicitly supports) that builds against the old SPI will fail to load with `AbstractMethodError` or `java.lang.Error: Unresolved compilation problem`, depending on how the SPI is loaded. The PR does not call this out as a breaking change in the description, and there is no default implementation (e.g. derived from `getId()`) to keep existing extensions working.

findings.title: postInit shortcut-collision check is incomplete
findings.body: The post-startup validation only asserts `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()`, which detects duplicate shortcuts among grants but ignores the reserved shortcuts declared in `AccessTokenContext.SessionType` (`on`, `of`, `tr`, `un`) and `AccessTokenContext.TokenType` (`rt`, `lt`, `un`). Notably, `RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT = "rt"` already coincides with `AccessTokenContext.TokenType.REGULAR.getShortcut()` ("rt"), making the encoded id and the lookup maps ambiguous on inspection. The same applies to `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN = "na"`: a custom grant using `"na"` as its shortcut would silently overwrite the UNKNOWN entry rather than being rejected at startup. A stronger startup assertion verifying (a) every grant shortcut has length 2, (b) no grant shortcut collides with any `SessionType`/`TokenType`/`UNKNOWN` shortcut, and (c) the maps have matching sizes would catch these classes of foot-guns before any token is issued.
